about: Where the port may differ from .NET Framework's System.Web.DataVisualization, and why. DataVisualizationParityTests: in a case matching 'case', the lines matching 'line' (the golden's and the port's) are set aside; what remains must be equal. An entry that sets aside no difference (on its platform: 'all', 'windows' or 'linux') fails the test: it is stale.

differences.reason: The chart's assembly version, which BuildNumber reads: the port's is FrameworkOnCore's (10.0.29.0, as every assembly of FrameworkOnCore's WebFormsForCore), .NET Framework's 4.0.0.0. Only the property shows it (not the saved settings, not the page).

Culture data: on Linux .NET has ICU's (percents with 3 decimals, ja-JP's currency sign the full-width U+FFE5), not Windows' (NLS: 2 decimals, U+00A5), which this program asks for on Windows (UseNls). Converted applications on Linux get the original server's instead (the culture profile made into ICU data by the deployment); the chart formats with whatever the culture says.

The layout follows the text's measure: Liberation Sans (Arial's widths, not its hinting) moves the pie a few pixels, and the slices' arcs are flattened into other points. samples/ChartProbe (experiments/wf4c/chart-probe.ps1 -Linux) compares a page's image map with IIS's: within 5 pixels.
The annotation is sized to its text as measured: Liberation Sans, not Arial (the height 9.81 for 9.32).
The port records no metafile into a stream: the chart's EMF, EMF+ and dual formats write nothing.
Without a web application the handler's folder is the temporary folder (Path.GetTempPath): /tmp/ on Linux, the user's Temp on Windows. The rest of the settings are the same.

differences.line: ^\s*\|\s+<NamedImage |^saved again equal = |^!! escaped: System\.ArgumentNullException: Value cannot be null\. \[param encoder\]$|^binary =
differences.reason: The chart's images as the port writes them: a PNG with other chunks and compression (Skia's encoder) in the saved XML, the same bytes again once read back (GDI+ writes a read PNG otherwise), and a bitmap made in memory written as PNG where GDI+ has no encoder for it (the binary format's save: ArgumentNullException on .NET Framework and on the port on Windows).
